title: The Lee Resolution and the Move Toward Independence
learningObjectives: Identify the sequence of decisions following the proposal of independence in 1776
Explain how the Lee Resolution led to separate plans for treaties and confederation

explanations.text: The Lee Resolution proposed three distinct actions that shaped the work of the Second Continental Congress.

evidence.quote: The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."

explanations.text: Approval of the resolution's parts occurred gradually over more than a year.

evidence.quote: The plan for making treaties was not approved until September of 1776; the plan of confederation was delayed until November of 1777.

events.label: Second Continental Congress meets in Philadelphia

evidence.quote: Its second meeting convened in Philadelphia in 1775.
New York cast no vote until the newly elected New York Convention upheld the Declaration of Independence on July 9, 1776.

events.label: Richard Henry Lee introduces independence resolution

evidence.quote: On June 7, 1776, Richard Henry Lee of Virginia, introduced this resolution in the Second Continental Congress proposing independence for the American colonies.
On June 11, 1776, the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution:
